reaction: Back to the valley. Last time the driver could not hold Insist on Maryam. That test is what I came back for, plus whether the cutting beats the rain.

input.name: Call the hamlet to cut the landowner’s barley

reaction: Same opening. I know the call works, so I make it straight away and spend my attention on the delayed ones.
Waiting for replies, no Skip.
Zehra is reaping her own barley first. Fair. I do not insist on a fair reason. Waiting for the rest; I am looking for Maryam.
Nothing moved in fifteen seconds. Last time the count rose to 18. Only 6 answered so far. Çoban has a filled dot; I am checking whether that dot marks the delay.
Zehra asks who will feed her family. So Send grain is the answer to her, and it costs me slack. I hold off and see if more replies come.

Second time in. I called at once. 5 came, 1 delayed (Zehra of Çoban, reaping her own barley, asking who feeds her family), nobody refused. Fewer answers than last time at this point, and the count has not moved for half a minute. Clock still 18 July. The dot on Çoban seems to mark the delay this time. I have the Insist, Visit and Send grain choices in front of me and want finally to test the hold.
Before I spend Zehra’s goodwill, how much is cut so far?
Nothing cut yet, 360 standing, two days to rain. Six of perhaps two dozen answered. I will run the test I could not run last time: insist on Zehra and watch what she remembers.

input.name: Hold to insist on the work This person will come and will remember that you insisted.

reaction: Selecting the insist button first so I can hold it with the keyboard.
Same message as last time. Holding Enter on it now, a second and a half.
It went through. The insist button disappeared and Çoban’s dot went from filled to hollow. No line saying she agreed or what she thinks. Checking About.

Zehra will soon give birth. I pressed a pregnant woman to cut the landowner’s barley, and the information was one tap away under About. That is on me; I read the reply and not the house. ‘Your record: you pressed Zehra (today).’ It still says 1 delayed. Now I watch whether she actually comes and whether cutting starts.
“I’m coming. Don’t stand over me.” Clear consequence, clear voice. Insist works and costs something I can see. Now Demirci, Kuyucu and Tepe have filled dots. Back to the overall replies.

Six more, all the same sentence: reap our own barley first. If insisting just works, it is the obvious move every time and the only cost is a grudge. I want to know if 11 cutters finish 360 before the 20th without pressing anyone else. Waiting to measure the cutting.
Thirty seconds, nothing in the notebook changed and the date is still 18 July. Checking the ledger for cut barley.
About 1 measure cut, same as last time at this stage. I want to see the rain bar.

Screenshot: about eleven dots in the landowner’s field, so the cutters are there. The rain bar is maybe seven percent filled, red rain mark around eighty-five percent. At this pace the real wait to rain is many minutes. I will sample cutting again after a wait.
Waiting with the notebook open.
The insist test finally ran and gave me a real answer with a real grudge. But now I am back to watching a date that does not move, waiting to learn whether 15 cutters are enough.
15 came, 7 delayed now. Measuring cut again.
About 5 cut, 350 standing, after roughly 45 real seconds more. Tepe has three people delayed, the most of any house. This time I read the house before I press anyone.
Only one Tepe insist here although three were listed in the notebook. Reading About.

All three of Tepe are delaying, and the son is a coffeehouse type. Insist moves one person and leaves a grudge. My hypothesis: a visit moves the whole house. Last visit cost two real minutes for ‘Come in.’, so this is a deliberate test, not a hope.
Walking up the slope. Waiting.
Arrived at Tepe faster than Demirci last time. Again nothing to say or choose. Waiting for the visit.
“Steward, sit down if you’re staying.” A line, but no choice for me and the delays have not changed. Dere just got a dot. I am waiting, the same as last time.
Requested phone check, not my choice. Sitting at Tepe anyway.
Phone check: one ordinary tap, About on Tepe.

Phone check 315 to 320 s: map a thin strip, house row cut at both edges, About text pushed under the fixed visit status and buttons, so the jars-looked-low line is hidden below the fold. Insist button large and readable. Back to desktop. The visit result is again the same: jars low, my guess they will delay for their own barley. The visit did not move them.

Visit gave me a reason, not a result: jars low, barley at home first. The fair answer to low jars is grain, but every measure I give is gone from a six-measure slack. I want to see what Send grain asks before committing.
“A small sack.” How small? With six measures of slack I will not spend an unknown amount. Not sending. I want the cutting number first.

Granary 24. It was 30. So that one tap on Send grain actually sent six measures. I read the text as a description of what it would do and decided not to. My entire slack is gone in one tap: 24 + 25 + 330 = 379 against 384. I am now five short on paper. Insist needs a hold; giving away grain needs nothing. That is backwards for me.
If I paid six measures, I want to know at least whether it bought anything at Tepe.
No line at Tepe about grain arriving. Correction to my note: I am only guessing the six measures went to Tepe. I never saw ‘sent’. Checking today’s news.
“I came when you insisted. Look what happened to me.” What happened? She is pregnant. That line lands hard and I have no idea what it refers to. And now 1 refused. Going to Çoban.

I would leave here. Two consequences in a minute and I cannot see either cause. Six measures left the granary on what I took for a description, and Zehra says look what happened to me with no line saying what. I came back to test insist, and the test answered, but now I am behind on grain and guessing. I keep playing to see if her harm is ever explained.
About first, in case it says what happened to Zehra.
Nothing explains it. She came, then she refused. I will walk to Çoban when I am back; that is the only way I see to find out.
Zehra’s line made me care about the people more than the barley, which is not what I expected, but the grain loss without confirmation makes me distrust my own inputs.
Back at the residence. Visiting Çoban to find out what happened to Zehra.
Walking down to Çoban.
Tepe’s dot went hollow, like Çoban’s did after insisting. Did the grain or the visit move them? Checking while I sit at Çoban.

“That is kind of you. We’ll keep it for spring.” Confirmed: the grain went to Tepe, a minute and a half after I tapped. And they are keeping it for spring, not eating it so they can cut. So my six measures bought gratitude, not labour. Do the three still delay?

Correction: Tepe 3 came, 0 delayed. Visit plus grain moved the whole house, where insist moved one person and cost me Zehra. Six measures for three cutters. That is a trade I can reason about, now I see it. I still do not know if the visit alone would have done it. Back to Çoban, where I am sitting.
Sitting with Çoban. Waiting for whatever they say.
Yusuf: “Sit down.” Nothing about Zehra. The answer must be in About again, if anywhere.

“They have almost no food left.” So Zehra’s first answer was literal: who feeds my family. I pressed a pregnant woman from a house with no food. Still no word on what happened to her. Sending grain is the decent answer, and I am already five short. This is the hard choice I wanted, but I made it worse by not reading first. Checking the ledger before I decide.

40 cut + 320 standing + 24 granary = 384 exactly. Earlier 379 was rounding in the ‘about’ figures. So I am not short, I am at zero. Rate: about 15 cut in two and a half real minutes. I will not send Çoban grain; at zero, any gift is a shortfall. That is a cold call and I know it. Next test, one variable: visit Kuyucu without grain, to see if the visit or the sack moved Tepe.
Waiting to get back to the residence.
Thirty seconds with the ledger open: still 40 cut, still at Çoban. Same as last time. I think the ledger holds the day. Closing it.
Notebook open, waiting to walk back.
Walking back. 17 came now. Still 18 July after nine real minutes.
I am learning something real about insist, visit and grain, but each test costs a minute or two of walking with nothing to do, and the date has not changed in nearly ten minutes.
Back. Kuyucu for the visit-only test.
Visit only, no grain. If Kuyucu comes, the visit did it at Tepe too.
Walking.
At Kuyucu. Sitting.
“We weren’t expecting you.” Waiting to see whether the dot changes without grain.
A minute at Kuyucu, dot still filled. Checking About for their state.

Result: visit alone, my guess is still ‘would put it off’. At Tepe the guess changed to ‘would come’ only after the grain. So grain is the lever, the visit only shows me the jars. That is a clean answer and I like it. Also Çoban’s dot just went filled again. Checking.

Now Yusuf delays too, same reason. Grain would probably move him. The real question is whether I need more cutters at all, and I cannot answer that: I do not know how fast the field goes against the rain. Six measures for three cutters is only a good trade if those cutters save more than six from the rain. Going back to watch the bar.
Walking back.
It is afternoon now in the news. I want to compare the rain bar with the one at 156 seconds.

Bar: a solid stretch then a hatched stretch to about a fifth, rain mark near 85 percent. My rough guess: rain in another forty real minutes, the field at this rate needs about an hour. So I need more cutters and I cannot pay grain. Insist is what is left. Reading Demirci before I press anyone this time.
Who lives here?

input.name: Hold to insist on the work This person will come and will remember that you insisted.

reaction: A smithy, five people, nothing fragile written about them. Repeating the insist under different conditions: does a sturdy house take it better than Zehra did?
Holding.
Pressed one at the smithy. The ‘Keep holding’ hint stays on screen even after it worked, which made me doubt it for a second. Waiting for the answer.
Two insists, two different answers: Zehra resentful, the smith ‘I’ll do as you say, steward.’ Conditions matter, so insist is not a free move. That is what I wanted to find.
Zehra’s complaint came about four minutes after she came. I will watch whether the smith’s son says anything later before I press again.
Watching the news.
Maryam of Çoban now in the delayed list, the 68-year-old mother. Last time it was a Maryam I wanted to press. I am not pressing a 68-year-old from the house I already hurt. Checking the cut.

90 cut, 270 standing. From 40 to 90 in about five and a half real minutes, roughly double the earlier rate now that 21 are out. At that pace the field needs under half an hour; my rough rain guess was forty minutes. So it may just make it without pressing anyone else. That is the first time I feel I can plan rather than guess.
Letting the cutting run. Watching for the smith’s house to say anything.
Nothing new. I have my answers on insist, visit and grain. What is left is waiting for the field.
Fifteen minutes and still 18 July. I would stop here for tonight. Looking at Feedback first, selecting only.
Opening Feedback to look only.
“I’m stopping” is there in those words. Selecting it locally. Typing nothing, submitting nothing.

Stopping at 907 seconds, 18 July, afternoon, with the feedback open. I pressed I’m stopping; it put those words in the note box by itself. I typed nothing and submitted nothing. I got my answers: insist works with a hold and its cost depends on who you press, a visit shows the need but grain is what moves a house, and the cutting may beat the rain. What is left tonight is fifteen to thirty more minutes of watching 18 July. I would come back another evening to see whether the field is cut and what Zehra meant. I would not leave it running. The browser is no longer needed.
